# Park and resume against a rate-limited upstream

The upstream answers `429` and asks you to come back later. You want the node to wait out the limit and try again, not to fail, and not to burn a retry budget on a wall-clock guess.

Rimsky spells this as a **park**: the run stops occupying a dispatch slot, keeps its identity, and comes back on a schedule the upstream chose. The bundled `http-node` executor does it for you — a `429` with an unexpected status parks the node and takes the resume instant from the response's `Retry-After` header.

## The shape

- The node runs on `http-node` and does not list `429` in `expect_status`.
- The executor parks the run and rimsky records a `transient/park` signal carrying the resume instant.
- No dispatch slot is held while the run is parked. The park roster names it.
- At the resume instant, the same run reaches the upstream a second time and settles on that answer.

## The template

```yaml
name: rate-limited-fetch
version: "1"
description: Fetches from an upstream that rate-limits, parking on 429 until the upstream says to come back.
nodes:
  - type: fetch
    executor: http-node
    max_runtime: 1h
    max_retries: 3
    retry_backoff:
      kind: exponential
      base_delay_ms: 1000
      max_delay_ms: 30000
    error_types:
      "http/timeout":
        action: retry
      "http/network_error":
        action: retry
      "http/server_error/500":
        action: retry
      "http/request_invalid/quota_exhausted":
        action: give_up
        reason: upstream quota exhausted for this key
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:
            type: string
            default: "https://api.example.com/v1/items"
          method:
            type: string
            default: GET
          expect_status:
            type: array
            default: [200]
          count:
            type: integer

  - type: store
    executor: http-node
    subscribes:
      - node: fetch
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: fetch
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    error_types:
      "http/server_error/500":
        action: retry
    max_retries: 3
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:
            type: string
            default: "https://sink.example.com/v1/store"
          method:
            type: string
            default: POST
          count:
            type: integer
            source: "{{nodes.fetch.attribute.count}}"
```

`fetch` needs no park declaration. It parks because the upstream answered `429` and the node did not say it expected one.

`count` is declared on `fetch` with neither a `source:` nor a `default:` because the executor writes it: `http-node` turns a JSON response body into the node's attributes delta. Declaring it is what lets `store` name it — a substitution reference must name a key the sender declares.

## What you will see

The node emits one `transient/park` tagged `rate_limited`, carrying a `resume_at` derived from the upstream's `Retry-After`. It resumes by itself, runs a second time, and succeeds against the cleared upstream. The response body becomes the node's output attributes verbatim, so `{{nodes.fetch.attribute.count}}` downstream reads a field of the JSON the upstream returned.

While it waits, the park roster names it:

```
rimsky parked list --instance <instance-id>
```

Each row gives the node, when it parked, and when it is due back. `GET /v1/admin/diagnostics/parked-nodes` returns the same roster.

## Sharp edges

**Listing `429` in `expect_status` cancels the park.** A node that expects the status treats the answer as an ordinary success and settles `terminal/success` on it. That is the flag that decides whether you get parking at all.

**You cannot subscribe to a park.** `transient/park` is audit-only: it writes to the ledger and fires no cascade. Registration rejects a subscription against it, with a message telling you to subscribe to the eventual `terminal/success` or `terminal/error/<class>` instead. Wire downstream work to the outcome, never to the park.

**An upstream that moves during the park discards the parked run.** If a node upstream of the parked one re-runs while it waits, rimsky does not wake the parked run and carry it forward. A wake is recorded, a **different** run dispatches with inputs re-substituted from the freshened upstream, and the parked run never settles. The upstream sees the newer value, not the value the parked run was holding. Where nothing upstream moves, the parked run does resume on its own inputs and reaches the upstream carrying the same body. Plan for the first case: do not treat a park as a durable hold on the inputs the executor saw.

**Parking is per-executor, not a platform feature.** `http-node` parks on `429` and `claude-agent` parks on its own rate-limit class. The two verifier executors do not park. The stub-mode attributes that force a park — `probe_park`, `probe_cancel`, `park_resume_at` — register cleanly on any executor, and reach a parked node only on `http-node` and `claude-agent`, and only when the operator set `RIMSKY_EXECUTOR_STUB_MODE=1` on the executor process. You cannot rehearse this graph offline by declaring them.

**`max_quiet_period` and `max_runtime` still bound the run.** A park is not exempt from the node's deadlines. A `max_runtime` shorter than the upstream's `Retry-After` ends the run before it resumes.

**The outbound guard is closed by default.** `http-node` blocks loopback, private, link-local — the cloud metadata address included — unique-local, and multicast destinations, checked on the resolved address at connect time, so a redirect to a private address is blocked too. Open a range with `RIMSKY_EXECUTOR_HTTP_NODE_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST`; a malformed entry fails the executor's boot.

**The error class comes out of the response body.** An unexpected status returns a class read from the response's `error_class_field`, which defaults to `error_class`. A body naming no class falls back to `..._unspecified`. Set `error_class_field` per node when your upstream names its errors under a different key.
